correctness.rationale: For an unbounded generator, every sufficiently right resolvent is non-Fredholm because its range is the dense proper domain of the generator. Uniform nilpotence of noninvertible Calkin elements therefore makes the mth power of each resolvent, hence of each Yosida approximant, compact. The Yosida powers converge strongly to the identity. If L is the short-time operator-norm limsup, every c>L is a valid global exponential-bound prefactor after a semigroup-law blocking argument; the resolvent estimate then gives limsup norm of the Yosida approximants at most c. Thus compact approximants of asymptotic norm at most c^m exist, and optimizing c down to L proves the inequality. Boundary cases beta=infinity and beta=1 are consistent.

value.rationale: The result converts a new qualitative Lotz/BCAP criterion into an intrinsic quantitative obstruction: the best compact-approximation norm forces a minimum short-time operator-norm jump for every nonuniform semigroup. This distinguishes finite BCAP coefficients rather than merely the binary presence or failure of BCAP, and it recovers the focal theorem at the infinite endpoint. The coefficient is natural and already central in quantitative approximation theory; the conclusion directly controls semigroup geometry rather than merely improving a disposable constant in an intermediate estimate.
